evidence: Declared page prerequisite of the canonical plan and of the batch-20 manifest. The actual in-run item uses are the hook/border-strip items recorded in the two item rows below; no other batch-19 item is consumed. Supplier page owned by the batch-19 pair of this run; e-core/rim-hook block material of the same source is deliberately deferred to the batch-21 cores page, so only the hook/border-strip interface is owed here.

Required claim: a removable border strip of lambda is a connected rim set with no 2x2 block whose removal leaves a Young diagram, with its size and height. Used in the proof route of the Gram determinant item to state Lemma 5.26's evaluation of the exponent d_mu(beta_1,...,beta_b+h_ab,...,beta_c-h_ac,...): unwrapping the rim hook R^lambda_ac and re-wrapping it with lowest node in column b, with the sign (-1)^{l_ab+l_ac}. Supplier homed on the batch-19 page; supplier manifest item is scaffolded, not yet authored. Not independently verified here.

Required claim: the bijection between nodes of [lambda] and removable border strips, with the strip of a node having size equal to its hook length and height equal to its leg length. Used to identify the source's rim hook R^lambda_ab (size h^lambda_ab, leg length l^lambda_ab) with a removable border strip, which is what licenses the displacement/evaluation statement in the Gram determinant item. Supplier homed on the batch-19 page (scaffolded, not yet authored). Not independently verified here.

Required claim: removable border strip with size and height. Used for the index interpretation of the Jantzen sum formula terms: the virtual symbol indexed by (beta_1,...,beta_b+h_ab,...,beta_c-h_ac,...) is the class obtained by moving the (a,c)-rim hook of size h^lambda_ac to column b, as in Lemma 5.26. Supplier homed on the batch-19 page; declared in the consumer's deps. Not independently verified here.

Required claim: hooks of lambda correspond bijectively to removable border strips with size = hook length and height = leg length. Used to identify the moving strip in the Jantzen sum formula with the hook of the source's Lemma 5.26 and with the hook lengths appearing in the coefficients nu_pi([h^lambda_ab]_qhat) - nu_pi([h^lambda_ac]_qhat). Supplier homed on the batch-19 page. Not independently verified here.
